text:
alex: Quick dump — repro and perf traces for a weird KV slot identifier drift we hit in prod. Long context chats (~8-12k tokens) sometimes end up with wrong slot IDs after a batch-split, causing stale blocks to be referenced across requests and slow mem growth (~20-30MB per 1k tokens). Attaching logs below.

maria: Can you paste minimal repro and the exact command you used? :eyes:

alex: repro steps:
```
# start runtime in dev mode
./run_local_runtime --kv-pages=256 --batch-split=auto --log=debug
# run long-context client
python tools/repro_long_context.py --length 10000 --threads 2
```
logs: see snippet below (trimmed)
```
[2026-11-03T13:04:12Z] kv: alloc slot_id=1024 ctx=38
[2026-11-03T13:04:12Z] kv: write page idx=12 offset=4096 tag=0x7f23
[2026-11-03T13:04:12Z] kv: evict candidate slot_id=1024
[2026-11-03T13:04:13Z] kv: allocate slot_id=1024 ctx=41  <-- reused id but different ctx
[2026-11-03T13:04:13Z] request 0x7f23: read page idx=12 tag=0x7f23  // stale data served
```

ryan: Hmm, looks like slot_id is a simple counter reused on free but we expect eviction to clear tag->slot mappings. Any chance batch-split merges are racing with evict tombstones? I saw a similar pattern when batching heuristics split mid-request.

sylvia: I ran perf trace on local and saw that continuous batching path triggers a fast-free path that skips zeroing when under load. Kernel selection change last week also changed memory fence ordering (GPU memcpy->async). Could be combined.

perf-bot: Profile summary (alloc/free trace):
```
allocs: 34k
frees: 33.7k
active slots: 300
heap delta over 10k tokens: +220MB
hot path: kv_write -> slot_map.insert (20% time)
```

maria: Does the repro require two concurrent requests? Or single long request?

alex: Repro is flaky single-request with long context, much higher with concurrent feeders. Also more likely when batch-split triggers a zero-length tail batch (fast path).

ryan: I added asserts in a local branch: check slot.tag == expected_tag before reuse and log if mismatch. Reproduced quickly. Pushing to PR and linking issue.

dev-bot: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/3421|issue #3421> created by ryan: "kv: slot id reuse leads to stale block reads after batch-split". CI job 542 queued.

sylvia: Proposed fix: on free, increment slot generation counter and require generation match on read. Also add a memory barrier after free before reuse (addresses GPU async fence). Might cost a bit but prevents correctness bug.

alex: Agree on gen counter + assertion. Also add regression test: reproduce pattern with batch-split set to force split per token and long context.

maria: Also check batching heuristics: we might be creating zero-length continuation batches that trip the fast-free path. If we avoid that pattern we might reduce incidence until fix lands.

ryan: My PR includes:
- assert guard in slot allocator
- small fence on reuse for GPU memcpy path
- new test repro_long_context_flaky.py

perf-bot: Quick benchmark of guard on dev box: latency +1ms p50, mem steady vs leak. Worth it as stopgap.

alex: Thanks. Assigning: ryan to PR, sylvia to kernel fence check, maria to add regression test in CI, I'll follow up with load-run in staging. Marking issue as high-priority. :thumbsup:
